test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?
A detrimental circumstance or detail; a drawback.
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **A fly in the ointment**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"A fly in the ointment"** refers to a detrimental circumstance or detail that spoils or reduces the overall enjoyment or effectiveness of something. (किसी चीज़ में बाधा डालने वाली समस्या) • **Example:** The project was almost flawless, but the delay in delivery proved to be a fly in the ointment. • The phrase signifies that despite the overall positive aspects, there is a small drawback that diminishes the value or effectiveness. (छोटी समस्या जो बड़ी चीज़ को प्रभावित करती है) • **Example:** While the party was enjoyable, the lack of proper seating arrangements was a fly in the ointment. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **A fly in the ointment**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **A fly in amber** (एम्बर में फंसी मक्खी): This phrase generally refers to something preserved forever in time and unable to change. • **Example:** The ancient insect trapped in amber looked like a fly in amber. • **A fly on the wall** (दीवार पर मक्खी): This idiom means to be an unnoticed observer of a situation or event. • **Example:** I wish I could be a fly on the wall during their private conversation. • **A fly on the wheel** (पहिए पर मक्खी): This phrase refers to someone who believes they have significant influence, but actually, their presence or actions are inconsequential. • **Example:** He tried to dictate the terms, but he was just a fly on the wheel in the grand scheme of things. 207:T97b, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **To surprise someone who is normally alert, shrewd, or on-guard.**.
